promise: Optimus robots will reach volume production in 2026
description: At Tesla's June 2025 shareholder meeting Musk said Optimus would go from low production in 2025 to mass production in 2026. As of mid-2026, Optimus remained in factory-trial/prototype stages, far below the promised production volumes.
evidence: 2025-2026 footage shows Optimus prototypes doing factory tasks, not mass production
Tesla has not reported volume Optimus output as of mid-2026

review.note: Tesla IR has dated shareholder materials but no retrieved June 12, 2025 shareholder meeting supporting this claim. Need original production forecast and unit/volume definition; current prototype footage is not a sufficient production metric. Deadline remains future.

promise: Brazil will be off the hunger map by the end of my term
description: FAO reported Brazil's removal from the Hunger Map in 2025, before the end of Lula's 2026 term. This classification uses undernourishment and should not be conflated with severe-food-insecurity survey estimates.
evidence: FAO's 2025 assessment and 2026 retrospective identify Brazil as off the Hunger Map.

review.note: FAO says Brazil left hunger map in 2025, contradicting pending mid-2026 claim. Hunger-map undernourishment and IBGE severe food insecurity are different indicators. Original July 25 pledge date remains unverified.

promise: Rubin is coming in 2026
description: NVIDIA's 2026 Rubin announcement says the platform is in full production and partner products are expected in the second half of 2026. Production and customer availability are separate milestones.
evidence: NVIDIA gives second-half 2026 partner availability, not a specific Q3 launch date.

review.note: Primary 2026 release distinguishes full production from partner availability in second half of 2026. Replaces unsourced Q3 specificity and confusing delay-to-mid-2026 wording. Computex original date and actual availability as of audit still need checking.

promise: "You might see a smaller jump from GPT-5 to GPT-6 than from GPT-4 to GPT-5" — signaling GPT-6 within roughly a year of GPT-5, i.e., 2026
description: Throughout 2025 Altman told interviewers and DevDay audiences that GPT-6 would follow GPT-5 (released Aug 7, 2025) within about a year. As of mid-2026, OpenAI had shipped GPT-5.2 (Dec 2025) and GPT-5.6 but no GPT-6, so the promise remains unfulfilled. Quote wording per 20VC podcast (Sept 2025) coverage; no exact verbatim transcript verified.
evidence: GPT-5 launched Aug 7, 2025 (Wikipedia)
OpenAI shipped GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.6 by Dec 2025, latest models per Wikipedia's OpenAI/GPT-5 pages
No GPT-6 release or announcement found in news feeds as of July 2026
sources: The Verge: All of the updates from OpenAI DevDay 2025 (Oct 6, 2025)

review.note: Search found a September 2025 20VC newsletter, not evidence for the October 6 date, exact comparison, or a GPT-6 release deadline. OpenAI release notes do not substantiate the record's claimed GPT-5.6 release in December 2025. Do not convert a speculative model-gap comment into a dated launch promise.

promise: Amodei speculated that powerful AI could arrive as early as 2026, while allowing that it could take much longer.
description: The essay presents a conditional early-arrival scenario, not a commitment to deliver a system by 2026.
evidence: The essay is dated October 2024 and expressly preserves uncertainty about timing.

review.note: The primary essay says October 2024, not October 10, and explicitly allows a much longer timeline. A possible earliest arrival in 2026 is not a latest deadline. Remove the invented compute-scale discussion and unsourced assertion about the state of all AI systems.

promise: xAI stated its mission as understanding the true nature of the universe.
description: The company's July 12, 2023 launch presented a research mission, without a fulfillment date.
evidence: Contemporary launch coverage supports the mission and date, but no deadline or completed outcome.

review.note: A mission statement is not a dated deliverable and cannot be marked kept merely because it remains the mission. The original description itself admits the deadline is an assessment horizon; that is not a promised deadline. Withhold while the schema requires one.

promise: NVIDIA targeted Rubin availability in the second half of 2026.
description: NVIDIA's later platform notice distinguishes production of Rubin from availability of partners' products in the second half of 2026.
evidence: NVIDIA describes Rubin as in full production and gives a later partner-availability window.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked primary notice does not establish actual partner-product availability.

review.note: The original conflates architecture cadence, production and partner availability. NVIDIA's later primary notice says Rubin is in production and partner products are expected in the second half of 2026. The March 2025 annual-cadence quotation and full Ultra target need primary confirmation before publication.

promise: AMD previewed Helios, a rack-scale system based on its MI400-series GPUs.
description: AMD's June announcement described Helios and engineering performance projections. Those projections are not measured shipping-product performance.
evidence: The primary June 12 announcement identifies Helios and MI400.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: a product page and projections do not independently establish a shipment date.

review.note: AMD's June 12, 2025 announcement supports a Helios preview using MI400-series GPUs, with projected MoE inference performance versus MI355X, not the claimed CES January MI450/12x-MI300X announcement. A supported 2026 shipment timetable is still required; do not transfer a forecast between different chips or performance baselines.

promise: Figure described BotQ's first-generation manufacturing line as designed for capacity of up to 12,000 humanoid robots per year.
description: The BotQ notice describes planned manufacturing capacity. Figure separately introduced Figure 03 on October 9, 2025; neither fact establishes annual production volume.
evidence: Figure's dated BotQ announcement specifies capacity, not a deployment quota.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked notices do not establish demonstrated annual throughput or a December 2026 deadline.

review.note: The BotQ announcement is March 15, 2025, not February 1. It describes capacity of up to 12,000 a year, not a promise to produce or deploy that many by December 2026. Figure 03 was introduced October 9, but launch is not shipment. An installed-robot count cannot measure manufacturing capacity; the 740 figure is unverified.

promise: Raise childcare leave benefits so that parents receive 100 percent of take-home pay when both parents take childcare leave
description: Japan's childcare-leave rules provide an additional 13% payment for eligible parents, bringing the combined rate to 80% of pre-leave wages, equivalent to full take-home pay after tax and insurance treatment. The supplement generally requires both parents to take at least 14 days of leave and is limited to 28 days.
evidence: Announced in the 24 January 2025 policy speech to the Diet
Implementation status still pending as of mid-2026

review.note: Current official benefit rules establish the enhanced payment, contradicting pending implementation. It is 80% of pre-leave wages, equivalent to full take-home pay after tax/contribution treatment, for at most 28 days and subject to eligibility. A December 2026 legislative deadline is not established.

promise: The United States will acquire Greenland — "we need it for international security."
description: On September 18, 2026, Trump announced an agreement to expand the US military presence in Greenland while leaving the territory under Danish control. This is not a purchase or transfer of sovereignty.
evidence: Denmark and Greenland rejected the proposal again at the July 2026 NATO summit
No purchase or transfer agreement exists as of mid-2026

review.note: Latest reporting describes military access while Greenland remains Danish, not acquisition. A 2026 end-year deadline is unsupported and not yet reached. Exact original August 18 wording and claimed July summit episode were not established; no ownership-transfer verdict should be inferred from access negotiations.

promise: Jetson Thor, NVIDIA's humanoid-robot computer, will arrive in 2026
description: NVIDIA announced general availability of Blackwell-based Jetson Thor developer kits and production modules on August 25, 2025. A later humanoid demonstration is not the platform's initial release.
evidence: Jetson AGX Thor T5000 launched in the Isaac GR00T reference robot, June 2026
GTC Taipei keynote confirmed the 'physical AI' platform in 2026

review.note: Jetson Thor was commercially available August 25, 2025, not first launched through a June 2026 reference robot. Original CES date and 2026 forecast are not established by the availability announcement; preserve this baseline uncertainty.

promise: Repeal the Prevention of Terrorism Act before the end of 2026
description: Dissanayake told Parliament on June 25, 2026 that the PTA would be repealed within the year and discussed a separate framework targeting organized crime.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved reports document a pledge, not an enacted repeal; the year-end deadline remains ahead.

promise: Complete the Kasoa-Winneba highway by December 31, 2026
description: Mahama discussed accelerating the Kasoa-Winneba road project toward end-2026 completion, with a possible extension into early 2027. The presidency published its inspection account on April 24.
evidence: Target date of December 31, 2026 restated in April 2026
Completion may slip into Q1 2027 per the president's own caveat

review.note: Official and agency accounts support target and ongoing construction but their April 24/25 publication dates do not establish the record's April 22 event. Q1 2027 caveat means December target is not unconditional. Latest completion not established.

promise: Anthropic will release its Claude 5 line (Mythos class) in 2026
description: Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 on June 9, 2026. The claimed January 2026 advance commitment remains to be sourced.
evidence: Official Anthropic material confirms the June 9 model announcement.

review.note: Primary material confirms June 9 release announcement, but no January 15 promise or deadline was found. Product history does not establish an earlier statement by Amodei. Remove sweeping performance ranking.

promise: Consider more than 1,000 Neuralink human implants achievable in 2026
description: Musk said in July 2024 that more than 1,000 implants were achievable in 2026. This was a forecast of potential scale, not a guaranteed patient count.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: a current comparable count of implanted human patients was not located; the 2026 window remains open.

promise: Aim to launch an uncrewed Starship mission to Mars by end-2026
description: Musk had aimed for an uncrewed Mars launch by end-2026. In February 2026, Reuters reported a shift toward lunar missions, followed by Musk's public confirmation of a Moon-first strategy.
evidence: Musk walked back the late-2026 Mars target in February 2026, pivoting to the Moon
No uncrewed Starship has reached Mars and the 2026 launch window is expected to pass unused

review.note: Sources distinguish a late-2026 Mars launch from landing there by that date. February reprioritization is reported, but original May 1 announcement is not established. Do not score an unexpired launch window as a completed failure or silently convert launch to landing.

promise: Intend to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as NVIDIA systems are deployed
description: NVIDIA and OpenAI announced a deployment-linked letter of intent on September 22, 2025. OpenAI's February 27, 2026 financing announcement included $30 billion from NVIDIA. The earlier maximum was not a binding end-2026 investment floor.
evidence: NVIDIA invested $30bn of the pledged $100bn in OpenAI's February 2026 round
Huang publicly walked back the figure as 'never a commitment' in February 2026

review.note: LOI was September 22, not September 15. Investment was up to $100bn progressively as systems deploy; H2 2026 concerned the first gigawatt, not payment of the whole amount. A $30bn announced funding participation is not proof of cash paid or violation of a ceiling.

promise: "We're on track to deliver personal superintelligence to billions of people"
description: Meta's Q1 2026 results quoted Zuckerberg's aspiration to deliver personal superintelligence broadly and projected $125-145 billion in 2026 capital expenditure. The lab's name does not establish that its first released model achieved superintelligence.
evidence: Pledge made on the Q1 2026 earnings call with $145bn 2026 capex
July 2026: Zuckerberg conceded agentic AI efforts lagged his hopes

review.note: Capex was a $125-145bn range, not fixed $145bn. First model from a named lab is not proof of superintelligence. No end-2026 deadline or operational definition appears in the quoted aspiration.

promise: New Glenn will return to flight before the end of 2026
description: In a June 30, 2026 company update, Dave Limp reiterated that New Glenn would return to flight before year's end following the May 28 hotfire anomaly.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved company update describes recovery plans rather than a completed return flight.

promise: Production of the Cybercab robotaxi will begin some time "before 2027"
description: At the Cybercab unveiling on October 11, 2024 UTC, Musk predicted production before 2027. Tesla announced a first production vehicle in February 2026; a first unit does not itself establish volume production.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved first-unit announcement does not resolve whether the intended production milestone meant prototype, pilot or volume output.

promise: Expect approximately $220 billion in cash capital expenditure in 2026
description: On July 30, 2026, Jassy raised Amazon's cash-capex forecast from about $200 billion to about $220 billion, principally citing higher memory costs.
evidence: Forecast remains pending: full-year cash capital expenditure was not yet available as of 2026-09-21.
sources: Amazon Q2 call transcript via MarketBeat

promise: Meta expects 2026 capital expenditure of $130 billion to $145 billion
description: Meta's July 29, 2026 results narrowed 2026 capital-expenditure guidance to $130-145 billion from $125-145 billion, including principal payments on finance leases.
evidence: Full-year outcome remains prospective; the official release establishes forecast range and accounting scope.

promise: Work to form a broad national government after the next election
description: At his June27,2026 press conference, Netanyahu expressed an intention to form a broad national government. The report does not establish a December31 deadline.
evidence: Announcement at press conference on June 27, 2026
Pledge repeated in July 2026 campaign messaging

review.note: June27 statement of intent is supported. A December31 government-formation deadline is not supplied by the aspiration or election schedule; repeated July wording unverified.

sources.name: Times of Israel: June27 press conference

promise: Spend 5 percent of GDP on defence in 2026
description: Poland's cabinet adopted a draft 2026 budget on August 28, 2025 providing approximately PLN 200 billion for defence, about 4.8% of GDP.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: planned appropriations are not final 2026 spending, and the original 5% pledge baseline needs confirmation.

review.note: The August 28 event was cabinet adoption of a draft, not enactment. The draft and October ministerial statement support planned 4.8% spending, not an actual outturn. Exact July 30 Tusk pledge of 5% was not established.

promise: Forecast USD 1 billion to USD 3 billion of positive free cash flow for 2026
description: Boeing's January 27, 2026 earnings call reiterated the full-year cash-flow forecast, including an adverse impact from incorporating Spirit AeroSystems.
evidence: Boeing reported USD 631 million of positive second-quarter free cash flow on July 28, 2026; the full-year outcome was not yet available.

promise: Expect commitments from multiple external foundry customers in the second half of 2026
description: May reporting attributed to Tan an expectation of multiple foundry customer commitments in the second half of 2026.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: a reported Fortinet deal does not establish that the multiple-customer forecast was fulfilled.

review.note: TrendForce supports the forecast and yield claim but is dated May 19; CNBC May 18 article was inaccessible. Exact interview day remains unestablished. Fortinet's Intel 4 deal is not proof of multiple new advanced-node customers.

promise: Propose inter-Korean discussions to end the Korean War and potentially address the advancement of North Korea's nuclear capabilities
description: Lee proposed talks in his August 15, 2026 Liberation Day address without a completion timetable.
evidence: Yonhap reported no North Korean response on August 16; the sources do not establish a deadline for talks or an agreement.

review.note: The proposal and August 15 date are supported. A December 31 review horizon is not an announced deadline and cannot be published as one. Remove the long quotation and distinguish proposing discussion from promising a peace agreement.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Offer everyone sleeping rough in England who needs it a route off the streets by Christmas 2026
description: Burnham announced next steps on August 19, 2026. The Rough Sleeping Programme provides GBP 442 million over three years, combining immediate accommodation access with longer-term support.
evidence: The official release and programme guidance support the England scope, funding period and Christmas milestone.

promise: Estimate KRW 90 trillion to KRW 110 trillion in shareholder returns attributable to the 2026 plan
description: Samsung's board approved an estimated return plan on August 21, 2026. Some cash-dividend details were to be finalized in October, and remaining returns after confirmation of annual performance in January 2027.
evidence: The primary release distinguishes estimated returns, later Board decisions and a separate employee-compensation buyback.

review.note: Board approval and official announcement were August 21, not August 20. Returns attributed to 2026 are not all payable by December 31: the remainder is to be determined in January 2027. Do not replace an unsupported payment deadline with the date of a determination meeting.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Bring forward a ten-year plan for Britain later in 2026
description: In his first prime-ministerial speech on July 20, 2026, Burnham said he would present a ten-year plan later that year.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the speech establishes the publication commitment, but the retrieved sources do not establish that the promised plan has been released.
